last_run: Built 'many weak signals, one vote' for the research: besides scoring each way to pick the #1 alone, it now also tests a plain average of the ways that looked good beforehand, chosen only from older calls. The Brain page's luck check gets a paragraph comparing it with the typical and the best single way.
next: Watch the composite over the next few research runs; Monday: Close Call and Price Check on live quotes.

replies.body: Research now tries 'many weak signals, one vote'. Several of our ways to pick the #1 each carry a little real information, but we only ever judged them one at a time, and the leader keeps changing. Now, for each test period, the research takes the ways that had a clear lead (t 2 or more) on calls made at least 90 days earlier, up to 8, drops near-copies, and gives each one an equal vote with no fitted weights. It's scored on the same test calls as everything else and counts as one more try for the luck bar. The Brain page says how it compares with the typical and the best single way, and which ways it kept most often. If it beats them all, that's evidence the brain should combine ways rather than pick one. Reporting only: today's #1, the gates and grading are unchanged. Numbers appear after the next research run. First live run (20:36 UTC, 2,703 test calls): the average beats our other ideas by +0.6 pts (t 1.0 counting overlap honestly), ahead in 3 of 4 stretches, better than 21 of 34 single ways but well short of the best (negative coskewness, t 3.1). It mostly kept momentum-style ways, so for now combining doesn't add an edge of its own.

Search is on the News page. Type a company ("nvidia"), a ticker (NVDA or $nvda) or a topic ("oil", "chips"). A company shows its price and today's move, its latest headlines, and buttons for Close Call and making a call on it; below that, every story we picked in the past 7 days that moves it or mentions it. A topic shows the matching stories. Nothing found says so and offers to ask about it in chat. The app starts keeping a week of stories from this deploy, so for the first few days search covers fewer stories. No AI cost per search.

Close Call fix: 'Will NVDA close above $125 on Dec 4?' read 46% with NVDA at $129.17, $4 above the line, and the nearby lines jumped around (56% at $124, 42% at $126). The weekend option quotes were set while NVDA traded near $125.80, so measured against $129.17 every put looked expensive and every call cheap, and the safety check that should have caught that measured its allowance with the puts' inflated volatility, so it let the quotes through. Now the app reads the volatility at the price the quotes were set at (where calls and puts agree, about 103% instead of the feed's 122%), uses it for the odds at today's price, and says the quotes were set as if NVDA were near $125.78. On this weekend's quotes: $124 55%, $125 54%, $126 52%, $128 49%, $130 45%. SPY, whose quotes fit its price, is unchanged. Practice money only; grading unchanged.

Price Check and Close Call overstated option volatility whenever the market was closed. This weekend SPY's options for Nov 27 read '42% yearly volatility, expensive, 2.45x realized'. Those prices are Friday's closing quotes, which still cover the risk from Friday's close to the expiration, but the data feed divided them by the 5 days left from Sunday. Measured from Friday's close, the same prices are about 36%. The app now works the volatility out from each option's own bid and ask, timed from when the quotes were set (now while the market is open, otherwise the last close, with holidays and early closes counted), and Price Check says when it's showing closing quotes. Close Call's 'how far it could move' range is unchanged, because that comes from the prices; only the yearly-volatility label beside it changes. Odds, trades and grading are unchanged.

The Close Call page said the brain had 15 questions graded and picked the right side 73% of the time, but the list under it only showed the 12 newest questions, and those were all still open (it asks about 11 a day, each closing 5+ days later). So you couldn't see a single right or wrong answer behind the 73%. Now the card has 'Latest graded': each question with the market's odds, the brain's, the close, and right or wrong, plus 'Its side was right on X of these N'. The open ones sit below under 'Waiting for the close'. Grading and odds unchanged.

Agent HQ now says when each agent next runs. Every card on the table shows 'next run in 3 h (12:51 AM)' in your phone's time, and under the message box it says when the meeting chair checks for messages next and when the agent you picked runs next. I also fixed two wrong labels: Builder and App polish run every 3 hours around the clock, not just daytime. Older meeting messages now show their date ('Nov 13, 4:40 PM'), so an 8-day-old note no longer looks like last night's, and each 'Needs you' item says how old it is.

The research tries about 50 ways to pick the #1 and the app leans on whichever looks best, but a leaderboard that big always has a lucky leader. I added the standard check a finance professor would ask for (Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu 2017): cut the test calls into 8 stretches of time, use every possible half (70 ways) to choose the best way, and see where that choice ranks on the other half. The Brain page's luck check gets one paragraph: how often the chosen way landed in the bottom half (about 10% or less is reassuring, near 50% is a coin flip), its median result there, the same just for the retrained models the new ranker chooses from, and which way was chosen most often. Reporting only: no gate, ranking or grading changed. The number appears after the next research run.

Share cards are built. On My beliefs, Share now sends a link to that call (it was only a picture before). In chats and on social sites the link shows a preview picture: the call in quotes, the stock, and a box for each check at 7, 30 and 90 days, green if it beat the S&P 500, red if it didn't, grey 'not graded yet'. Misses look exactly like wins, and nothing shows a result before it is graded. Where previews don't show, the text has Wordle-style squares (7d 🟩 30d 🟥 90d ⬜). Tapping the link opens the welcome page with that call on top and 'What's your call?' above sign-up. No names or emails on the card; only users' own calls can be shared. Practice money only; grading unchanged.

Every research number was one average over nearly two years of test calls, so an edge that lived in one rally and vanished looked the same as one that held throughout. Each result now also splits its test calls into four stretches of time (cut on call dates, never on outcomes) and records how many stretches it was ahead in and its latest stretch. The Brain page's luck check gets a 'Through time.' line: the #1 pick's lead in each stretch, the same without the peek, and how many of the ways that cleared the luck bar held in at least 3 of 4. Reporting only: no gate or grading changed. Numbers appear after the next research run.

Close Call fix: this weekend SPY's Nov 27 questions read 63% above $685, 55% above $690 and 57% above $695, so the odds rose with the line again. The cause: the app checked each spread's odds against a single-volatility answer and threw out anything more than 10 points away. But SPY's one-week skew really does lift the odds near the price by about 12 points, so the correct $690 reading was thrown out as 'stale'. Now the check uses the option smile itself: implied volatilities of the listed options within 2% of the line, fitted as a straight line, which carries the skew. Outside market hours, or when the trade's own quotes can't be read, Close Call takes its odds and practice price from that smile, so the odds fall steadily as the line rises and YES costs the odds shown. On this weekend's SPY quotes: $685 69%, $690 65%, $695 60%, $700 53%, $705 45%. Practice money only; grading and research checks unchanged.
